artworks.title: The Anger of Achilles
artworks.description: David's Achilles at the moment of the false marriage — the bridegroom named in Agamemnon's lie when Iphigenia came to Aulis.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia (Pompeii fresco)
artworks.description: Pompeian fresco of the Aulis altar — Iphigenia borne toward the knife while Artemis' deer waits as the substitute.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Tiepolo's Villa Valmarana fresco — Agamemnon averting his eyes as the fleet's wind-price is paid at Aulis.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Doyen's French academic staging of the Cypria/Euripidean rite — the princess on the altar so the ships may sail for Troy.

artworks.title: The Sacrifice of Iphigenia
artworks.description: Steen's Dutch Baroque Aulis — crowd, priest, and victim packed into the moment before Artemis' intervention.
